title: Smith-Morra Gambit Accepted | The Sensei Speedrun | GM Naroditsky

moves.spoken: A pretty high-rated opponent at seventeen-ninety-three — let's see how our repertoire fares. e4, c5.
d4 — we've been playing the Smith-Morra exclusively.
Black takes and we offer the gambit pawn with c3 — the Morra gets more exciting at this level, because people tend to accept and play conventionally.
Black accepts, d takes c3, and we recapture with the knight on c3 — a big lead in development for the pawn.
Black develops the knight to c6.
The knight to f3, developing the other knight.
Black plays e6 — one of many possible systems.
The bishop goes to c4 regardless — it's an exception to the usual rule, because from c4 it supports a knight sacrifice on d5 and makes it hard for Black to play d5.
Black develops the bishop to c5.
The big-picture rule is to develop your kingside and castle quickly — so we castle.
Black plays a6, which is quite inaccurate — the d6-square is very important, and it becomes hard for him to ever push d6.
The bishop to f4, clamping down on that d6-square.
Black plays the knight to e7, contesting d6.
A logical plan is a bishop on d6, so we push e5, seizing space and squeezing the square.
Black castles.
The knight shifts to e4, adding another attacker to d6 — look at the control we've built over that square.
Black retreats the bishop to a7.
Now we switch gears and keep improving — the queen to d2.
Black plays the knight to g6 — not scary. The bishop to g5 would hit the queen, but keep the bigger picture in mind.
We're trying to keep our e5-pawn well defended, so we calmly drop the bishop to g3.
Black plays b5 — and the knight on g6 is actually quite misplaced, with an h4-h5 idea to exploit it.
The bishop steps back to b3, out of harm's way.
Black plays the queen to b6 — I don't like that move at all for him.
The only thing Black might be preparing is the knight to d4, so we bring the rook to d1 to prevent it and get into the game.
Black plays the bishop to b8 — and good thing we tucked our bishop to b3 earlier.
Now everything is in place and we can start attacking — the queen to g5, with knight checks on f6 also worth considering.
He made it easy for us, but the knight to g5 would have been possible — so let's check the theory of the line.
